title: Name a borrow lifetime
summary: Add lifetime parameters to a borrowing struct and a function that returns a reference.

scenario.briefing: A telemetry excerpt stores a borrowed string, and a longest helper returns one of two borrowed strings. Neither declaration says how long the borrow lasts. Add the lifetime relationships the compiler needs.

objectives.description: Add a lifetime parameter to a borrowing struct.
Choose the declaration for a struct that stores a reference.
Explain elision, 'static, and borrow checking accurately.

hints: A struct that stores a reference needs a lifetime parameter.
The longest function needs one lifetime shared by both inputs and the output.
Use <'a> on the struct and the function.

misconceptions.description: Storing a reference without declaring its lifetime.
misconceptions.testDescription: The excerpt struct declares a lifetime for its borrow.
misconceptions.feedback: A borrowed field needs a named lifetime so the struct's validity can be checked against the borrowed data.
'static requires the data to live for the whole program. A normal struct should borrow for its own lifetime parameter instead.

misconceptions.description: Believing lifetime annotations change runtime behavior.
misconceptions.feedback: Lifetimes are erased during compilation. They only describe and check borrow validity.

sections.title: A lifetime is a validity bound
sections.body: A lifetime parameter tells the compiler how long a reference must remain valid. It does not create or extend storage. A struct that stores a reference declares a lifetime so the struct cannot outlive the borrowed data.

sections.title: Elision rules cover common cases
sections.body: Rust infers lifetimes in simple signatures: one input reference gives the output the same lifetime, and a method with &self gives the output the lifetime of self. When a function has several inputs and returns a reference, the relationship must be written explicitly.

sections.title: 'static means the whole program
sections.body: 'static describes a reference that can live for the entire program, such as a string literal. It is not a fix for a borrow-checker error. Most data should be tied to the scope that owns it, not forced into static storage.

steps.explanation: Lifetimes are compile-time validity bounds. Elision covers simple cases, 'static is the strongest bound, and the borrow checker enforces the relationship.
